newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon begins new evacuation phase from Sierra Leone. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pentagon begins new evacuation phase from Sierra Leone. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: The United States began a new phase of evacuations of Americans and other nationals from a new site in Sierra Leone following reports of violence at the original pickup site, the Defence Department said on Tuesday.
"We began another phase of the evacuation from Freetown," Lt. Col. Nancy Burt said. "It's a beachfront area, a beachfront restaurant." She said she did not have additional details on the location.

Burt said there were a few Americans and other nationals involved in the third (corrects from second) round of evacuations following last week's rescue of more than 1,255 (corrects from 900) Americans, foreigners and some deposed government officials after a military coup.
All U.S. evacuees in last week's operation were taken from Freetown's Mammy Yoko Hotel to the nearby warship, the USS Kearsarge, via U.S. Marine helicopters.
But Burt said reports of violence at the hotel prompted the rescue to begin from a new site. She said that was the only change between the first and second phases of the evacuation.
"Everything will be the same. The only difference is we're picking people up from a different location because the situation (at the hotel) had deteriorated over the last few days.
"We've heard reports of fires and there's been fighting in the area."

CH-53 "Sea Stallion" helicopters, which can carry up to 55 passengers, and CH-46 "Sea Knight" helicopters, capable of carrying 22 passengers, were being used for the latest evacuation as they were in the first.
"We have 561 (corrects from 182) evacuees on the ship ... and we expect to evacuate in the neighbourhood of 600 people," Burt said.
She said the operation was going "quickly" and that it would end in a few hours.
